name: Wells Score for Deep Vein Thrombosis (modified, 2003)
condition: Leg pain or swelling (possible blood clot)

citations.text: Wells PS, Anderson DR, Rodger M, et al. Evaluation of D-dimer in the diagnosis of suspected deep-vein thrombosis. N Engl J Med. 2003;349(13):1227-1235.

validated_population: Outpatients with suspected deep vein thrombosis of the leg.
self_report_note: The score was validated with clinician examination. One item (whether another diagnosis is at least as likely) requires a clinician and is not asked; it is scored 0, which is the cautious choice.
license_note: Published clinical score; not a copyrighted instrument. Question wording is original to OLA BOT.

red_flags.question: Do you have sudden shortness of breath, chest pain when breathing, or are you coughing up blood?
red_flags.help: A clot may have traveled to the lungs (pulmonary embolism).

red_flags.question: Is the leg cold, pale, blue, or numb?
red_flags.help: This can mean blocked blood flow in an artery.

items.question: Do you have cancer that is being treated now, was treated in the last 6 months, or is receiving palliative care?
Is the painful leg paralyzed, weak from a nerve condition, or was it recently in a cast?
items.help: Includes stroke-related weakness in that leg.
items.trace_label: Paralysis, weakness, or recent cast on leg

items.question: In the last 12 weeks, were you in bed for 3 days or more, or did you have major surgery with anesthesia?
items.help: Hospital stays and major operations count.
items.trace_label: Bedridden ≥3 days or major surgery within 12 weeks

items.question: Is there tenderness along the deep veins — the inner thigh or the back of the calf?
items.help: Press gently along the inner thigh and the middle of the back of the calf.

items.question: Is the entire leg swollen, from thigh to foot?
Measure both calves 4 inches (10 cm) below the bony bump under the kneecap. Is the painful calf at least 1¼ inches (3 cm) bigger around?
items.help: Use a soft tape measure or a string. Choose Not sure if you cannot measure.
items.trace_label: Calf swelling ≥3 cm vs other leg

items.question: Press a finger into the swollen area for 5 seconds. Does a dent stay, and only on the painful leg?
items.help: A dent that stays is called pitting edema.

items.question: Are there new, visible surface veins on the painful leg (not varicose veins)?
items.help: New veins that stand out on the skin.

items.question: Have you ever been diagnosed with a blood clot in a leg (DVT)?
items.help: Only count clots confirmed by a test.

items.trace_label: Alternative diagnosis at least as likely (−2 if yes)

scoring.threshold_text: Score 2 or more = DVT likely; 1 or less = DVT unlikely (Wells 2003 two-level score).

likely.label: DVT likely
likely.interpretation: Your score means a blood clot in the leg (DVT) is likely. An ultrasound is needed to confirm or rule it out.

care.where_detail: Emergency department, or an urgent care clinic that has confirmed it can do a same-day leg ultrasound.
ed_redirect: Sudden shortness of breath or chest pain: call 911

unlikely.label: DVT unlikely
unlikely.interpretation: Your score means a blood clot is unlikely but not ruled out. A D-dimer blood test is the usual next step; a normal result rules out a clot when the score is low.
unlikely.recommendation: Get a D-dimer blood test within 24 hours.

care.where_detail: Urgent care or primary care clinic that can do a D-dimer blood test. Call ahead to confirm.
ed_redirect: Sudden shortness of breath or chest pain: call 911
